newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Maoming refinery resumes full operation.
newsitem.headline: China's Maoming refinery resumes full operation.

text.p: China's southern Maoming refinery has resumed full operations after Typhoon Sally forced a complete shutdown for about a week earlier this month, a refinery official said on Wednesday.
"We have resumed normal operations," a refinery planning official said by telephone.
The 8.5 million tonne capacity refinery in southern Guangdong province was forced to a complete halt after Sally cut off power supplies on September 9, he said.
"It was down for about a week," the official said, adding that the sudden stoppage of electricity had also damaged a pipeline in one of the plants.
While the official cited the production losses sustained during the week as being "very serious", he said the refinery had not increased imports of refined products.
"We had a sufficient stockpile, that was enough to supply demand during the period," he said.
The refinery, China's second largest, now runs at around 7.0 million tonnes per year, he said. Almost all Chinese refineries are customarily under-utilised due to the shortage of crude supplies.
